knowledge_units.context_summary: The study addresses the 'lab-to-fab gap' in organic solar cells by using slot-die coating with a green solvent to manufacture flexible PM6:Y6 devices. Power conversion efficiencies of 6.3% and 7.2% were achieved for binary and ternary devices, respectively. The text highlights the advantages of slot-die coating over spin-coating for scalable, roll-to-roll production.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces PM6 and Y6 as high-efficiency organic solar cell materials with complementary absorption spectra, suitable for scalable manufacturing. It details the fabrication of flexible, slot-die coated devices using a green solvent (o-xylene) without additives, achieving efficiencies up to 7% in ternary configurations. The devices demonstrate high stability, retaining over 99% of initial efficiency after 1000 hours of storage.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study characterizes PM6:Y6 organic solar cells using EQE, absorbance, and AFM measurements, noting strong absorption between 460 and 870 nm. It demonstrates the feasibility of slot-die coating on flexible substrates using a green solvent without additives. The results indicate that coating temperature significantly influences active layer morphology and device performance.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study investigates the impact of slot-die coating temperature on the performance of PM6:Y6 organic solar cells, finding that 100 °C yields optimal efficiency. While higher temperatures improve carrier collection and short-circuit current, they reduce fill factor due to edge aggregation caused by rapid solvent drying. Thermal annealing improves devices coated at lower temperatures but does not benefit those coated at higher temperatures.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study analyzes the impact of slot-die coating temperature on the performance of PM6:Y6 organic solar cells, identifying 100 °C as the optimal condition. Higher temperatures above 100 °C cause rapid solvent drying and material aggregation, reducing fill factor. Recombination analysis reveals that while bimolecular recombination is minimized at 100 °C, trap-assisted recombination remains the dominant mechanism across all tested temperatures.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The optimal coating temperature for PM6:Y6 solar cells was determined to be 100 °C based on power conversion efficiency, layer homogeneity, and the elimination of thermal annealing. Active layer thickness was optimized between 101 nm and 217 nm, with 217 nm yielding the highest average efficiency due to increased light absorption and reduced bimolecular recombination.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study identifies trap-assisted recombination as a dominant loss mechanism in open-air processed PM6:Y6 solar cells due to impurities and interface defects. Introducing PC61BM as a ternary component enhances electron mobility and creates an energy cascade that boosts short-circuit current and overall efficiency. The optimal ternary blend ratios tested were [1:1:0.2] and [1:1.1:0.1], with the latter achieving a slightly higher average power conversion efficiency due to improved fill factor.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study analyzes exciton dissociation and charge collection efficiencies in binary and ternary organic solar cells to explain performance improvements. It reports that adding PCBM enhances dissociation and collection probabilities, confirming better charge extraction in flexible, slot-die-coated devices. Stability tests show ternary devices retain 99.4% of initial efficiency after 1050 hours, while binary devices retain over 97% after 1500 hours.
